agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:415:Four runs after the fixes. Runs 1 and 3 changed the process preset; run 3 skipped the brim, said so, and added it when asked (`brim_type` auto_brim → outer_only). Runs 2 and 4 put the same changes on the one object as overrides (`target`), which is a wrong-scope selection and an eval failure against the pinned model. That happened although the descriptions and the `target` property already said that a selected object or a single-object project is not a request for an override; wording alone has not fixed it. The project's setup card, which reads Orca's own preset deltas, showed exactly Brim type auto_brim → outer_only, Enable support 0 → 1, On build plate only 0 → 1 (the preset already had `tree(auto)`), and the harness check `verify_support_settings_patch` reads the native Support-page fields back after the same patch with a dialog counter installed. The live regression (`--live-agent`) at this point: 21 requests, 4,275 to 8,683 input tokens, 58 to 92 per cent cached.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:417:**Regions (M5).** `region_annotate` resolves each row through `IWorkspace::plan_regions` at proposal (the card lists each label and what it will generate) and again at execution, then `apply_regions` removes the artifacts of replaced records and generates the new ones in one "Annotate regions" undo step; the coordinator writes the records to the product store. Geometry is stored in the mesh frame of one model part, so moving, turning or scaling the instance never unbinds a region; the object is found again by its id in the writing session and otherwise by name plus the facet count of each model part, so a record written before a save can find its object after a reopen (not yet exercised by a test). A face is found again as the Measure plane with the same normal, the same plane and the same area; a hole as a circle feature with the same centre and diameter. Holes are Measure's circular face borders, so a hole's depth is the distance to the matching mouth on the far side, or the part's extent along the axis for a blind hole; the blocker is a cylinder from the mouth inward, a millimetre larger all round and past each mouth because near the crown of a round hole Orca detects the overhang wider than the hole's own slice (a blocker the size of the hole left every support in place in the harness), and a reinforcing modifier is the hole plus 2 mm of wall. Kinds generate: support paint (`supported_facets`) and seam paint (`seam_facets`) through a headless `TriangleSelector`, colour paint for a material face, `SUPPORT_BLOCKER`/`SUPPORT_ENFORCER`/`PARAMETER_MODIFIER` volumes named `JusPrin rN ...` (how they are found again), and object overrides for reinforce or flexible on the whole object. Paint state is read back through a fork-owned `TriangleSelector` subclass, since the facet states are protected. Open paint gizmos are closed first, as the object list's "remove paint" does, because a gizmo writes its own copy of the paint back. `object_analyze` `regions` reports `bindingLost` and `artifactsMissing`; the shell harness proves Undo strands a record (artifacts missing, still bound), Redo restores it, a turn keeps it bound, and removal takes the artifacts away. `object_place`, `object_divide`, `object_merge` and `object_repair` list `regionsUnbound`: the regions bound before the call and not after.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:419:**Reshaping (M5).** `object_divide_preview` runs Orca's `Cut` (which works on its own copy of the object) or `ModelObject::split` / `ModelVolume::split` on an object in a scratch `Model`; the harness proves the revision, the undo history and the dirty flag do not move. The preview reports pieces as they would lie and an overhang area (downward faces steeper than the process's support threshold, excluding the bed face): an estimate, not a slice. It does not return an image yet; that lands with the image projection in M6. `object_divide` follows `GLGizmoCut3D::perform_cut` without connectors (snapshot "Cut by Plane", `InvalidateCutInfo`, `Plater::apply_cut_object_to_model`), refuses an object already cut with connectors, and splits to objects through `Plater::split_object(false)` on the selected object (the index overload is declared upstream and never defined; auto-drop off avoids its only question), or to parts through `ModelVolume::split` as `ObjectList::split` does. `object_merge` selects exactly the named objects in the object list and runs its assemble, which takes its own snapshot. `object_repair` runs the repair command's per-part CGAL step without its progress dialog, clears the object's paint as Orca does when it does not remap it, and changes nothing when no part has open edges. `enum_bitmask`'s `|=` does not compile for `ModelObjectCutAttributes` (it assigns a bitmask to an int); combine with `|`.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:421:**Slice checks (M5).** `slice_report` gains four sections computed from the plate's finished print on the GUI thread, gated on the object's `posSupportMaterial` / `posSlice` step as the preview gates its own drawing. supports: each support layer's footprint (`support_islands`, or `lslices` for BBS tree support, which does not fill `support_islands`; the toolpaths as a last resort) is intersected with the slices of every target at that layer's middle, taken with `slice_mesh_ex` under `PrintObject::trafo_centered()`: the cylinder or box of each bound `no_support` or `precision_hole` region, and a cylinder for every hole Measure finds in the mesh that no region names (each through-hole once). The target is shrunk by 0.2 mm first so support that only meets the rim is not "inside", and contacts under 0.5 mm² are dropped. seams: the result's `EMoveType::Seam` vertices (world coordinates, plate origin included), taken into each seam region's part mesh frame per instance and counted when within 0.6 mm of the region's facets. firstLayer: the first object layer's `lslices` area times the instance count, and `PrintObject::has_brim()`. islands: object slices that overlap nothing in the layer below (grown by 0.05 mm), with whether a support layer at most two layers under it reaches it. Face regions are not yet checked for support contact; only volumes are. The shell harness slices the T bar with normal supports, finds support inside the unannotated hole, marks it a precision hole and the back face hidden, re-slices, and proves the contact is gone and seams land on the back face.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:435:**Seeing and exporting (M6).** A tool activity may carry a `ToolImage` (base64 PNG or JPEG, capped at 1280 px and 2 MB) that is never persisted; the MCP projection appends an `image` content block (the bridge passes it through on every protocol version), and the OpenAI projection follows the function output with a user message holding an `input_image`, both tested. `view_render` calls `GLCanvas3D::render_thumbnail` with the main 3MF thumbnail's parameters (the plate's printable parts, no bed) and Orca's `Camera::ViewAngleType`, and encodes with `GCodeThumbnails::compress_thumbnail`; it refuses before the canvas is initialized, as the archive export does. Preview mode is not built. `project_attachment_read` reads only a relative path inside the attachment folder, outside `JusPrin/` and `.thumbnails/`; larger pictures are scaled and re-encoded with `wxImage`, text is cut at 32 KB. `slice_inspect` rebuilds the preview's layer split from `GCodeProcessorResult::moves` (the stored result has no layer list or layer times) and pages the plate's G-code file by line. `activity_cancel` is computation-only: a pending proposal through the coordinator's own cancel, the tools' slice through `Plater::cancel_slicing` (the notification's Cancel, which returns once the run stopped; the snapshot's running flag clears a moment later), and a tools' job through the worker's cancel, whose end is read from the jobs list. `export_file` writes G-code by copying the plate's slicer output (Orca's own export adds only post-processing scripts and removable-media handling, which this does not run), sliced and project 3MF through `Plater::export_3mf` with `Silence` (so the open project keeps its name and path), STL from the parts' raw meshes as placed (negative volumes are not subtracted), and presets through `PresetBundle::export_current_configs` with system presets included, because the presets in use are usually system presets with edits and Orca's menu would write nothing for them. `slice_start` takes `wait`, and `slice_report` an `intent` section that measures the slice against intent answers naming a time, a weight or a cost. The shell harness renders a front view, reads a packed picture scaled from 2000 px and a text file, refuses `..` and JusPrin's state, reads layers and G-code, writes all five export kinds without a dialog, refuses an unasked replace, a relative path and the data folder, and stops a running slice.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:445:**What the journey eval changed (M7).** `slice_report` findings follow Orca's send dialog: the bed-temperature advisory (which Orca never shows) and the older A-series copy of the traditional-timelapse warning are dropped, and the timelapse warnings carry `appliesWhen: "timelapse"` and are not critical, since a G-code export records no timelapse. An `export_file` card for G-code or a sliced 3MF names the slice's own warnings, and the result lists them as `sliceWarnings`. A refused call now names values outside a listed set and says when `project_open` got both `path` and `new`. The page's state push no longer shows the `project_open` that replaced the project inside the project it opened (the call is still live while it finishes; its record belongs to the closed session). Both adapters' instructions carry one shared sentence on how a print request goes (`kPrintJourneyGuidance`): record the intent, ask only consequential questions, record the plan and its assumptions with `plan_set` before changing the project, check the slice, export with `export_file`. The live regression (`--live-agent`) gained a plan stage: the real model queues two settings patches under one `planId`, the harness clicks the plan card's Approve all, and both apply in order with the second not stale.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:963:**Tools that read or write a caller-supplied path.** `project_open` and `object_import_file` read one; `export_file` writes one. A local process that can reach the socket can propose any of them, and none of them touches the path until the person approves a card that shows the exact path (and says "replacing it" when a file is there). Approval is per call; nothing is remembered. The coordinator tests prove the file is untouched on rejection for each: `project_open` (no open happens), `object_import_file` (no import happens), and `export_file` (an existing file keeps its contents after a rejection and is replaced only after an approval that named it). `export_file` is additionally destructive by class, so it can never use the computation-only exemption; it takes only an absolute path in an existing folder with the kind's extension, replaces a file only with `overwrite`, refuses OrcaSlicer's data folder and the project's temporary folder, and names a restrictive project license on the card and in the result. The shell harness writes all five kinds without a dialog and proves the refusals of an unasked replace, a relative path and the data folder. `project_attachment_read` takes no path: an id from the project's own attachment listing, resolved inside the attachment folder, with `..` and JusPrin's own state refused (harness).

agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:997:On 2026-09-16 it failed on Windows: `select_object(0)` returned false after `load_files`, seven checks failed, and the process died with `0xC0000005`. The test code was not stale. The cause was the machine setup. The Mesa provisioning script put `opengl32.dll` only in `mesa\`, where only the app launcher looks for it. A harness has no launcher, so this one ran on the system's GL 1.1 and its canvas never initialized. Selection is built from the canvas's volumes, so nothing could be selected, and the gizmo check then opened a paint gizmo with nothing selected. The script now also copies `opengl32.dll` beside each harness (see "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in [engineering-method.md](engineering-method.md)); re-run it on existing build trees. With GL in place, two harness faults surfaced that only Windows shows:
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:1000:- The data-directory cleanup threw, because the open log file cannot be deleted, and the uncaught exception turned a PASS into `0xC0000409`. It now warns instead, as the shell harness already did.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:1002:Pulling the script change does not fix a build tree that was already provisioned; run the script on it again. So that a tree without GL cannot fail this way unnoticed again, the harness now checks, right after its first model load, that the canvas initialized GL. If it did not, the harness stops with `HARNESS ERROR the 3D canvas did not initialize OpenGL` and the command to fix it, exits 1, and does not crash. A clean exit on that early path also needed the harness to close the main frame, as the shell harness does. It used to call `ExitMainLoop()`, which skips `MainFrame::shutdown()`, and a pending project backup then posted to the deleted frame.
agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:1028:Also run the shell harness with `--mcp` for direct HTTP, `--mcp-setup` for the isolated setup-command fixtures, no argument for normal shell regression, and `--stock` for stock behavior. `--manual-mcp <dedicated-temporary-directory>` provides a disposable two-plate fixture for real clients; do not use the user's normal data directory. Linux helper/launcher checks are documented in [the test README](../../tests/mcp/linux/README.md).

# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.
# JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

## Testing

```bash
npm test        # vitest: protocol, bridge client, reducer, and DOM interaction tests
```

The deterministic conversation scenarios (`/fail`, `/flaky`, `/slow`) are
implemented natively in `DeterministicMockAgent.cpp` and asserted by
`tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`; the tests here exercise the page against
a scripted mock host playing the same protocol.

### State matrices

`src/visual/` holds one state input per state on the Figma page **Agent UI ·
States & Components**: the approval cards, runtime and header states, chat
list, composer, messages, manufacturing history, the earlier-chat notice, and
the printer chat. Each is rendered by the production components, or by the
real `App` against a scripted host, so a state is covered only if real inputs
can produce it. `npm test` asserts every one renders; with an output path the
same test writes a review page of all of them at the 429 and 320 DIP dock
widths in both appearances:

```bash
PREVIEW_OUT=/tmp/agent-ui-states.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix
```

Open the page with `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` to narrow it to
the states being compared with a Figma node. The page proves rendering only;
look at the running app as well (`tests/shell`'s capture modes write PNGs of
the real WebView).

## Design

`tokens.ts` imports `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` at build time
and writes it onto the root element as custom properties: `--<group>-<name>`
for the semantic colors of the appearance the host reports, and, once at
startup, `--radius-<name>` for each radius plus `--font-<role>` holding the
complete `font` shorthand of each type role and `--font-code` for the one
monospace role, used only for code, keys, paths and IDs. `styles.css` may use only those variables for
color, radius, and type, and only the spacing scale (4 through 48) for
padding, margin, and gap; `styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
fails on any literal outside that contract, naming the offending line.

`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:


saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the

id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.
# JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

## Testing

```bash
npm test        # vitest: protocol, bridge client, reducer, and DOM interaction tests
```

The deterministic conversation scenarios (`/fail`, `/flaky`, `/slow`) are
implemented natively in `DeterministicMockAgent.cpp` and asserted by
`tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`; the tests here exercise the page against
a scripted mock host playing the same protocol.

### State matrices

`src/visual/` holds one state input per state on the Figma page **Agent UI ·
States & Components**: the approval cards, runtime and header states, chat
list, composer, messages, manufacturing history, the earlier-chat notice, and
the printer chat. Each is rendered by the production components, or by the
real `App` against a scripted host, so a state is covered only if real inputs
can produce it. `npm test` asserts every one renders; with an output path the
same test writes a review page of all of them at the 429 and 320 DIP dock
widths in both appearances:

```bash
PREVIEW_OUT=/tmp/agent-ui-states.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix
```

Open the page with `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` to narrow it to
the states being compared with a Figma node. The page proves rendering only;
look at the running app as well (`tests/shell`'s capture modes write PNGs of
the real WebView).

## Design

`tokens.ts` imports `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` at build time
and writes it onto the root element as custom properties: `--<group>-<name>`
for the semantic colors of the appearance the host reports, and, once at
startup, `--radius-<name>` for each radius plus `--font-<role>` holding the
complete `font` shorthand of each type role and `--font-code` for the one
monospace role, used only for code, keys, paths and IDs. `styles.css` may use only those variables for
color, radius, and type, and only the spacing scale (4 through 48) for
padding, margin, and gap; `styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
fails on any literal outside that contract, naming the offending line.

{"chunk_id":"bdf033","wall_time_seconds":0.000013584,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4146,"output":"# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)

Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.
# JusPrin Agent UI

The local React/TypeScript application that renders the Agent conversation
pane inside `wxWebView`. It talks to OrcaSlicer exclusively through the
versioned `jusprin-agent-bridge` JSON protocol whose shared source of truth is
`resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json`; the native side lives in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`.

The page renders native state and submits typed requests. It never owns an
editable copy of the project or conversation: the native `AgentHost` is
authoritative, and every reload re-runs the handshake and reconstructs the
page from the host's `state` message.

## Building

CMake builds this page whenever an input changes (`npm ci` from the lockfile, then `npm run build`). The output is `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; it is generated, not committed. Node/npm is required unless you configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply that file yourself.

```bash
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target jusprin_web
```

The bundle must stay a single self-contained file (`vite-plugin-singlefile`):
WKWebView does not reliably load `file:` subresources.

To point the running app at a Vite dev server instead of the packaged file (hot
module reload):

```bash
cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm run dev
JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://localhost:5173 ./build/arm64/src/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
```

Adjust the binary path for your build tree and platform. The environment
variable is read once at construction; there is no settings UI for it.

## Testing

```bash
npm test        # vitest: protocol, bridge client, reducer, and DOM interaction tests
```

The deterministic conversation scenarios (`/fail`, `/flaky`, `/slow`) are
implemented natively in `DeterministicMockAgent.cpp` and asserted by
`tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`; the tests here exercise the page against
a scripted mock host playing the same protocol.

### State matrices

`src/visual/` holds one state input per state on the Figma page **Agent UI ·
States & Components**: the approval cards, runtime and header states, chat
list, composer, messages, manufacturing history, the earlier-chat notice, and
the printer chat. Each is rendered by the production components, or by the
real `App` against a scripted host, so a state is covered only if real inputs
can produce it. `npm test` asserts every one renders; with an output path the
same test writes a review page of all of them at the 429 and 320 DIP dock
widths in both appearances:

```bash
PREVIEW_OUT=/tmp/agent-ui-states.html npx vitest run AgentUiStateMatrix
```

Open the page with `?show=<case>,<case>&mode=dark&dock=320` to narrow it to
the states being compared with a Figma node. The page proves rendering only;
look at the running app as well (`tests/shell`'s capture modes write PNGs of
the real WebView).

## Design

`tokens.ts` imports `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` at build time
and writes it onto the root element as custom properties: `--<group>-<name>`
for the semantic colors of the appearance the host reports, and, once at
startup, `--radius-<name>` for each radius plus `--font-<role>` holding the
complete `font` shorthand of each type role and `--font-code` for the one
monospace role, used only for code, keys, paths and IDs. `styles.css` may use only those variables for
color, radius, and type, and only the spacing scale (4 through 48) for
padding, margin, and gap; `styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
fails on any literal outside that contract, naming the offending line.
